url_strategy.approach: Two destinations only. Shopping placements -> product pages from the feed. All non-Shopping placements -> the custom kitchen funnel. Collections are organic-only.
url_strategy.shopping_placements: Product ads use the feed's own product URLs automatically. Nothing to supply.

non_shopping_placements.applies_to: Display, YouTube, Discover, Gmail and Search inventory within PMax -- everything that is not a product listing.
non_shopping_placements.rationale: Trevor's direction. These are browse-stage placements, not high-intent product searches, so a lead-gen funnel fits better than an arbitrary single product page. It also converts on lead form submission -- the one conversion action still firing in this account (18/30d).
non_shopping_placements.verified: Live final URL on 'Build Your Own Outdoor Kitchen Campaign', the account's only converting campaign.

feed_coverage_summary.rest_of_catalogue: The feed holds 894 eligible products overall. Everything outside islands/kitchens (pizza ovens 244, grills, fireplaces, components) is deliberately out of scope for this build -- see scope_decision.

scope_decision.focus: Outdoor kitchens only, segmented by brand: three asset groups covering 99 of 215 in-stock eligible SKUs.
scope_decision.reason: Trevor's call. The dropped groups had no matching image assets in the account (Pizza Ovens, Outdoor Kitchen Components) or only partial coverage (Built-In & Freestanding Grills -- Summerset only). Rather than launch asset groups with weak or borrowed imagery, PMax focuses on the one group with complete brand-matched image sets already in the account.
scope_decision.coherence: Also aligns the whole account on a single strategy: Search drives the custom kitchen funnel, PMax pushes kitchen products, Shopping covers the rest of the catalogue.
scope_decision.revisit: Pizza Ovens is the largest cluster in the feed (244 SKUs, Chicago Brick Oven alone 214). Worth reinstating as soon as imagery exists -- it is the biggest untapped opportunity in the account.

scope_note: PMax now serves ALL channels for this account -- it absorbs the Search and Shopping campaigns rather than running alongside them. Product ads route to product pages via the feed; search text ads and every other placement route to the custom kitchen funnel.

critical_settings.final_url_expansion: OFF — mandatory. Left on, Google routes traffic to whatever page it judges relevant, including the collection pages being deliberately removed from paid.
critical_settings.brand_exclusions: Consider adding, so PMax does not absorb branded search that would convert organically.

brand_breakdown_finding.question: Trevor asked whether PMax was broken down by brand. It was not -- the previous spec filtered on product_type only, lumping every manufacturer into one asset group.
brand_breakdown_finding.now: Three brand-level asset groups: Mont Alpi (47), Cal Flame (13), BetterPatio House Brands (39). 99 of 215 SKUs.

critical_gap.issue: 83 of the 215 islands/kitchens SKUs -- 39% of the category -- carry NO brand value in the feed.
critical_gap.severity: These are not cheap accessories. Price range $729 to $17,600, MEDIAN $10,999. It is the single largest and among the highest-value groups in the category.
critical_gap.consequence: No brand-based listing filter can reach them. They are invisible to brand-segmented PMax, and were equally invisible to the old brand-segmented Shopping campaigns.
critical_gap.fix: Populate the brand attribute in Merchant Center. This is worth more than any campaign restructuring -- it unlocks 39% of the category's inventory.
critical_gap.interim: Until fixed, they can only be reached by a product_type-based asset group, which forfeits brand-level control.

brand_breakdown_finding.second_finding: BetterPatio's own house inventory is fragmented across six brand strings: 'ufinish by betterpatio outdoor kitchens', 'betterpatio mountain series', 'betterpatio.com', 'betterpatio designer series', 'betterpatio', 'betterpatio unfinished outdoor kitchens'. Grouped manually here, but consolidating in the feed would be cleaner.

budget_split.note: Weighted toward image coverage and SKU depth. Cal Flame gets a strong share despite fewer SKUs because its imagery is the best in the account and it carries the highest price points.
